solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Underground location? Graves may be found here

definitions.meaning: a cellar is a room below ground level; the question mark flags the loose sense
Graves is a Bordeaux wine, stored in such a room, not a burial place

explanation.surface: A riddle about a burial place underground where graves are dug.
explanation.walkthrough: Graves, capitalised to hide it, is a wine from the Bordeaux region, so the second definition points to where bottles are kept, not bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar for wine is typically an underground storeroom where bottles such as Graves are kept.

clue.text: Coat of paint wife put on wood

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A decorator's wife applies a coat of paint to some timber.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put on' means placed above, so W sits on top of ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A wash is a thin coat of diluted paint or colour spread over a surface.

clue.text: English fellow's rising reputation

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a fellow is a man; the 's joins it to the next word

explanation.surface: An Englishman's reputation is on the up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns E + MAN so that it reads upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a name for oneself is to win a reputation, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Bossy sort who demands choice of TV channel?

definitions.text: Bossy sort who demands choice of TV channel?

parts.words: Bossy sort who demands choice of TV channel?
parts.note: a domineering person pictured literally as someone fixated on holding the remote handset

explanation.surface: A domineering person insists on picking what everyone watches on television.
explanation.walkthrough: The remote handset is often called the control, so someone obsessed with holding it is pictured as a person obsessed with controlling everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists on managing everything around them is idiomatically called this, and the remote is the TV control.

clue.text: Song introduced by army officer — it's ropy

indicators.note: the officer's abbreviation presents the song by wrapping round it, one letter on each side

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A soldier announces a song, which turns out to be poor quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ropy' in the surface means shoddy, British slang; as the definition it means made of rope. 'introduced by' puts ARIA between L and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a long noosed rope, so it is literally a ropy thing.

clue.text: Presenting the silver when interrupted by strife and noise

indicators.note: the silver symbol is split open by the other pieces placed between its letters

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
war is conflict or strife
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A prize-giving of silverware is disrupted by fighting and racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when interrupted by' splits the silver symbol; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Awarding a prize means formally presenting it to the winner, so the participles match.

clue.text: Are parliamentarians sorting expenses initially in recess?

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A question about whether MPs will deal with their expense claims during the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' looks like the parliamentary holiday; it is an alcove in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Unsophisticated friend keeps wanderin' about on island

indicators.note: the friend holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a pal is a friend
roving means wandering; the dropped g matches the apostrophe
c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A naive friend keeps roaming around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in wanderin' signals the clipped form with its final G dropped; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Provincial describes narrow, unsophisticated outlook, as of people away from the capital.

clue.text: Encouraging green sign — I must get moving

indicators.note: the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A green light signals that it is time to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges GREEN, SIGN and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Energising means filling with vigour, giving fresh impetus, close to encouraging.

clue.text: Student beginning to spurn female artist — 'heretic'

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist
an Arian followed the heresy of Arius about the nature of Christ

explanation.surface: A student starts to reject a woman painter as a heretic.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a well-known British artist; Arius was a fourth-century priest condemned as a heretic.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminarian is a student at a seminary, training for the priesthood.

clue.text: Last bit of crossword somebody finished

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: one means somebody, as in 'one does'

explanation.surface: Someone completes the final part of a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Done means completed or over, the same sense as finished.

clue.text: Striving to be successful and happy, one getting round in pub

indicators.note: the other pieces go inside the word for a pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
content means satisfied, happy
I is the Roman numeral one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone happy and competitive buys a round at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the happy word, one and round inside the pub word, after its first two letters; 'getting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in contention is still in the running, striving for a chance of winning.

clue.text: This could lead to baker performing acrobatic moves

parts.note: the word break, when its letters dance about, can produce the word baker

explanation.surface: An activity that might turn someone into a baker by doing gymnastics.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay, BREAK with DANCING as an anagram signal, leads to BAKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakdancing is a street dance style of spins, flips and other acrobatic moves.

clue.text: One may relax with a churchwarden

definitions.text: One may relax with a churchwarden

parts.words: One may relax with a churchwarden
parts.note: a churchwarden is also a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe, not only a parish officer

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds in the company of a parish official.
explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden is a parish officer, but also a clay pipe with a very long stem.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchwarden pipe is filled with tobacco, so someone relaxing with one is a smoker of it.

clue.text: Terminal strikes

parts.note: reads like industrial action at an airport, but means the final tolls of a bell for the dead

explanation.surface: Industrial action at an airport terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: Strikes here are strokes of a bell, and terminal means fatal or final.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is a bell rung for a death, its strikes marking an end, figuratively a fatal blow.

clue.text: Ladies trained to become models

indicators.note: trained letters are drilled and put into a new order

explanation.surface: Young women are taught to become fashion models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges LADIES. 'models' tempts as catwalk models; here it is exemplars.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect model or standard to aim at, so both plurals match.

clue.text: Accounts by means of verbal expressions

parts.note: in can mean by means of, as in 'paid in cash'
voices are spoken expressions of opinion

explanation.surface: Settling accounts by speaking rather than writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Invoices are bills sent to customers, a sense of accounts as statements of money owed.

clue.text: Impertinent female friend in Paris, dishonest type

parts.note: ami is French for friend
a liar is a dishonest person

explanation.surface: A rude woman's French friend turns out to be a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Familiar can mean overly informal or presumptuous, hence impertinent in manner.

clue.text: Being persistent, snatching a kiss outside

indicators.note: the first piece seizes the second and holds it inside

parts.note: eternal means everlasting, persisting for ever
X is the conventional symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: A persistent suitor steals a kiss out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snatching' puts X inside ETERNAL, after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: External means on the outside, an adjective as outside can be.

clue.text: Achieve two top grades having kept off the booze at home

indicators.note: the pair of grades holds the next piece between them

parts.note: A is the top grade, so two of them is AA
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
in means at home

explanation.surface: A student gets two As by staying sober at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having kept' puts TT between the two As.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal is to achieve or reach it, both transitive verbs.

clue.text: British before game the worse for wear

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: A Briton plays a game while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is a link word, putting B ahead of LOTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is slang for very drunk, and 'the worse for wear' is an idiom for drunk.

clue.text: What an expensive hired assassin will do in more ways than one

definitions.text: What an expensive hired assassin will do in more ways than one

parts.words: What an expensive hired assassin will do in more ways than one
parts.note: a costly contract killer both murders someone and earns a large sum of money

explanation.surface: A pricey hitman both does the job and profits handsomely from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means to make a big profit, and literally to carry out a murder; the hitman does both.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a large profit, while literally it describes committing a murder.

clue.text: Revolution in Italian city (not Italy's capital)

indicators.note: this word tells us to leave a letter out of the city

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An uprising in an Italian city that does not involve Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italy's capital' looks like Rome; it is the first letter, I.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn is one rotation, a full revolution of a wheel.

clue.text: Charity event making money over short time

indicators.note: the money piece goes over, covering, the time abbreviation

parts.note: a fee is money paid
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A fundraiser that makes money in very little time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts T inside FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fair, often held to raise money for a charity.

clue.text: Was aware of modern sounds

indicators.note: the word is said out loud and heard as another word

parts.note: new means modern

explanation.surface: Someone was familiar with the latest noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Knew is the past of know, so it means was aware of or familiar with.

clue.text: Issue showing senior police officer's commendation

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector; the 's adds S
a tribute is praise or commendation

explanation.surface: An official notice shows praise from a senior detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute is to give out or issue, both verbs of handing out supplies.

clue.text: Part inside petrol engine

indicators.note: signals that the answer is concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A component found inside a car's petrol engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' finds the letters running across 'petrol engine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is a part played by an actor, so part here is a stage sense.

clue.text: No drone can move in a systematic pattern

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: No unmanned aircraft can fly in a set formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges NO DRONE CAN; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordonnance is the systematic arrangement of parts in a building or artwork.
